datasets.label: Multi-date median · at least 3 valid dates
datasets.source: Derived from the 9 listed USGS Landsat 8/9 observations
datasets.method: Median of valid per-date weighted sun-exposed LST; requires ≥3 dates. Support fields report minima over contributing dates. Not a full-season average.
datasets.assumptions: Median of at least three valid observations at each extent. Contributing dates can differ by building; this is not a seasonal mean or a continuous record. No single observation-time sun angle or shade boundary represents this median. Stability tests keep the multi-day input fixed and vary outer weights, extent and recent/historical heat blend.
datasets.heat_use: Source evidence for the fixed multi-day H model

datasets.label: CSIRO summer 2018–19 · historical LST
datasets.method: CSIRO published LST (Kelvin − 273.15); nearest-neighbour reprojection to 30 m MGA55 analysis grid; area × distance weighted open ground at 50/100/150 m. No single-date shadow mask is applied to this historical mosaic.
datasets.assumptions: Historical context, not current weather or a trend. Contemporary footprint exclusions approximate present-day surroundings; buildings may differ from 2019. CSIRO retrieval differs from USGS Collection 2. Source QA and scene-by-scene contributions are unavailable in this delivered mosaic.

datasets.heat_use: Parent/evidence layer; derived CSIRO UHI enters the historical branch, not a second LST score term

context_sources.label: CSIRO 2018–19 surface urban heat island (UHI)
context_sources.description: Landsat-derived surface-temperature difference from an estimated non-urban vegetation baseline. Melbourne source scenes: 28 Jan and 24 Mar 2019. UHI is a temperature difference in °C, not absolute LST.
context_sources.role: One third of historical temperature context after percentile conversion; historical branch capped at 30% of H by default.
context_sources.coverage_note: 2,573 / 2,573 candidates have valid 100 m UHI context.
context_sources.limits: Historical mosaic; different retrieval from USGS Collection 2. No scene-specific pixel QA or per-date contribution map was supplied. It is not cooling, air temperature or a before/after evaluation.

context_sources.label: Victoria 2018 surface urban heat island · Mesh Blocks
context_sources.description: UHI18_M is a surface-temperature difference from a non-urban baseline. Assign one 2016 Mesh Block to each footprint interior point.
context_sources.role: One third of the historical temperature index after percentile conversion. No vegetation or canopy fields are loaded or scored.
context_sources.coverage_note: Downloaded 6,976 polygons across all five councils. 2,573 / 2,573 candidates have a unique polygon match.
context_sources.limits: An area value shared by buildings in a Mesh Block; not a building measurement. Missing or ambiguous matches remain unavailable. Source boundaries and heat predate the current inventory.
context_sources.attribution: State of Victoria; Department of Transport and Planning / DEECA

context_sources.label: Climate Victoria · monthly maximum-temperature normals, 1981–2010
context_sources.description: CSIRO Climate Victoria Maximum Temperature (3DS-M), version 4 (2020). Twelve monthly climatology rasters on a 9-arcsecond (~250 m) grid, representing near-surface air temperature about 1.2 m above ground. Based on station observations, spline interpolation, elevation and MODIS LST dependence.
context_sources.role: Mean of Dec/Jan/Feb 1981–2010 air-temperature normals, then percentile: one third of historical temperature context. All 12 months remain visible. Small climate differences can be amplified by ranks; this is an exploratory context term, not current heat exposure.
context_sources.limits: Only the 1981–2010 climatology archive was downloaded. The full 1981–2019 daily and monthly time-series archives are not loaded. This is a long-term normal, not a 2026 observation, indoor temperature or building-scale measurement.
context_sources.attribution: Stewart, Stephen; & Nitschke, Craig (2017): Climate Victoria: Maximum Temperature (3DS-M; 9 second, approx. 250 m). v4. CSIRO. Data Collection. https://doi.org/10.25919/5e5d9033d8cc7

method.assumptions: Scene-centre solar geometry, flat ground and vertical extrusions. Many building heights are estimated. No trees, terrain, facades or heat transfer are modelled. Neighbouring buildings beyond the study inventory may be missing. Geometry and image dates differ. At least three 30 m cells is an exploratory screening threshold, not proof that the native thermal sensor resolves this buffer.

peer_method_note: The peer report guided discovery of official historical heat sources. HEATSCAPE uses their temperature fields only and does not reproduce that report’s full composite. The exact source file, version and averaging interval behind its final map were not specified.
inventory_note: 9 unique Landsat scenes; each has ST_B10, QA_PIXEL, ST_QA and MTL. The extra Jan 6 MTL (1).txt is a byte-identical duplicate and is counted once. No original source files were modified. Files are recorded by name, size and SHA-256; derived model values are bundled locally for the public static site.

derived_displays.role: Selected-building map overlay only; no score changes
derived_displays.coverage: 2,573 candidates, 50/100/150 m; each uses its accepted Landsat dates
derived_displays.method: Union and intersection of date-specific display sampling masks. Polygon-only repairs and 0.1 m coordinate precision are display processing, not thermal resolution. Gold: all accepted dates; pale gold: some. These do not represent cloud-valid pixel footprints.
